#### ISI Report 2025

In September 2023, a new inspection framework was introduced which changed the nature of both the inspection itself and the report subsequently published. Instead of areas of the school being graded ('excellent' etc), the standards are either 'met' or 'not met'. I am very pleased to confirm that St Mary's met all the standards required, demonstrating full compliance. We are proud that so many areas of the school have been singled out for praise which reflects the quality of the education we provide across the board.

In order to reach their judgements, the 7-strong inspection team interviewed over ¼ of the student body, held meetings with 90 staff attendees (some staff had multiple meetings owing to various areas of responsibility), observed 25 registration and assembly slots, and visited around 100 lessons.

We are thrilled to share some of the report's key findings:

> "Leaders have a clear vision for school development based on effective monitoring and self-evaluation."

> "From early years and upwards, pupils show high levels of respect and tolerance. Consequently, behaviour is good and bullying is rare."

> "Boarding provision is carefully led and managed by knowledgeable and experienced staff. Conscientious supervision and a rigorous approach to safety ensure that boarders feel safe."

> "Teachers have a high level of knowledge and enthusiasm for their subjects."

> "Pupils feel safe and respected, with trusted staff always available."

[**Read the full report**](https://www.stmaryscambridge.co.uk/publications-and-media-galleries/reports.htm)

### Diocesan inspection report 2022

Our [Diocesan Inspection report](https://www.stmaryscambridge.co.uk/ugc-1/1/6/0/dea_final_report_st_marys_independen.pdf) undertaken by the East Anglia Diocesan Schools’ Service achieved the highest ‘**Grade 1’ rating of Outstanding** in all three areas assessed by inspectors in June 2022: Catholic Life, Religious Education and Collective Worship.  
  
Inspectors praised St Mary’s as: ‘_a school where everyone is respected and valued for who they are_’, with the quality of leadership described as ‘_extremely strong; it is both enterprising and aspirational_.’

> Inspectors reported _‘it is evident that the core Gospel values lie at the heart of life in school, clearly witnessed by the positive and caring relationships that exist between all groups.’_

[Read the full report](https://www.stmaryscambridge.co.uk/publications-and-media-galleries/reports.htm)

#### ISI Report 2025

In September 2023, a new inspection framework was introduced which changed the nature of both the inspection itself and the report subsequently published. Instead of areas of the school being graded ('excellent' etc), the standards are either 'met' or 'not met'. I am very pleased to confirm that St Mary's met all the standards required, demonstrating full compliance. # Why all girls'

*   Why all girls'

We excel at educating girls. From teaching and pastoral care to school life, everything at St Mary’s is built for girls.

Read**[The Top 10 list of reasons to attend a girls' school](https://www.stmaryscambridge.co.uk/ugc-1/1/50/0/the_top_10_list_of_reasons_to_attend.pdf?20250723_110722)**,as researched by the International Coalition of Girls Schools - it explains exactly why an all girl's educational environment works so well.

As a girls' school we enable girls to build self-confidence, alongside the knowledge and skills they need to reject and overcome gender stereotypes. Whilst academic results open doors for our girls, it is their self-belief, persistence and drive that keeps the door open.

### What we offer

*   Teaching tailored to girls’ learning styles, needs and developmental stage.
*   A space where gender stereotypes cannot thrive, where girls focus on being themselves and defining their place in the world.
*   A nurturing environment, full of role models that encourage and inspire girls.
*   Every opportunity for girls to take the lead; to be comfortable putting themselves forward.

### The facts

Statistics show that girls in single-sex schools achieve higher academic results, compared to their co-ed peers. We believe the benefits are much broader.

As members of the [Girls’ School Association](https://gsa.uk.com/schools/benefits-of-girls-schools/) (GSA), we offer an approach that empowers girls to pursue their unique path. Studies show that **girls in GSA schools**are more likely to choose ‘more challenging’ STEM subjects.

**Girls in GSA schools are:**

*   75% more likely to study Mathematics A Level
*   70% more likely to study Chemistry A Level
*   2.5 times more likely to study Physics A Level
*   twice as likely to study languages

> _"Free from stereotyping, our girls thrive in an environment that allows their intellectual and social confidence to flourish. They dream big - because here girls believe anything is possible. We understand ‘real-life’ isn’t single-sex and our education is well-balanced with the ‘co-ed’ life enjoyed by our students beyond our school gates."_**Hannah Helliar, Head**

### Learning styles

Girls and boys mature and learn in different ways. Research shows that girls prefer collaborative working and enjoy problem-solving, but tend to be more self-critical than boys. Our girls benefit from teaching tailored specifically to suit their learning styles, needs and developmental stage.

### Beyond gender stereotypes

Research also shows that girls in single-sex schools are less likely to follow gender stereotypes. They select subjects that they enjoy, based on their natural ability. Our girls think beyond stereotypes, combining Physics with Photography, Chemistry with Classics or Mathematics with Mandarin.

### Inspiring futures

Our girls do not view any career as closed to them. We encourage them to pursue their unique ambitions, supported by excellent careers advice and work experience opportunities.

### Taking the lead

In our small, girls-only classrooms, we offer an environment where intellectual and social confidence can blossom. This builds confidence. Our girls feel comfortable putting themselves forward, taking responsibility and leading.

*   Why all girls'

We excel at educating girls. From teaching and pastoral care to school life, everything at St Mary’s is built for girls.

Read**[The Top 10 list of reasons to attend a girls' school](https://www.stmaryscambridge.co.uk/ugc-1/1/50/0/the_top_10_list_of_reasons_to_attend.pdf?20250723_110722)**,as researched by the International Coalition of Girls Schools - it explains exactly why an all girl's educational environment works so well.

As a girls' school we enable girls to build self-confidence, alongside the knowledge and skills they need to reject and overcome gender stereotypes. Whilst academic results open doors for our girls, it is their self-belief, persistence and drive that keeps the door open.

### What we offer

*   Teaching tailored to girls’ learning styles, needs and developmental stage.
*   A space where gender stereotypes cannot thrive, where girls focus on being themselves and defining their place in the world.
*   A nurturing environment, full of role models that encourage and inspire girls.
*   Every opportunity for girls to take the lead; to be comfortable putting themselves forward.

### The facts

Statistics show that girls in single-sex schools achieve higher academic results, compared to their co-ed peers. We believe the benefits are much broader.

As members of the [Girls’ School Association](https://gsa.uk.com/schools/benefits-of-girls-schools/) (GSA), we offer an approach that empowers girls to pursue their unique path. Studies show that **girls in GSA schools**are more likely to choose ‘more challenging’ STEM subjects.

**Girls in GSA schools are:**

*   75% more likely to study Mathematics A Level
*   70% more likely to study Chemistry A Level
*   2.5 times more likely to study Physics A Level
*   twice as likely to study languages

> _"Free from stereotyping, our girls thrive in an environment that allows their intellectual and social confidence to flourish. They dream big - because here girls believe anything is possible. We understand ‘real-life’ isn’t single-sex and our education is well-balanced with the ‘co-ed’ life enjoyed by our students beyond our school gates."_**Hannah Helliar, Head**

### Learning styles

Girls and boys mature and learn in different ways. Research shows that girls prefer collaborative working and enjoy problem-solving, but tend to be more self-critical than boys. Our girls benefit from teaching tailored specifically to suit their learning styles, needs and developmental stage.

### Beyond gender stereotypes

Research also shows that girls in single-sex schools are less likely to follow gender stereotypes. They select subjects that they enjoy, based on their natural ability. Our girls think beyond stereotypes, combining Physics with Photography, Chemistry with Classics or Mathematics with Mandarin.

### Inspiring futures

Our girls do not view any career as closed to them. We encourage them to pursue their unique ambitions, supported by excellent careers advice and work experience opportunities.

### Taking the lead

In our small, girls-only classrooms, we offer an environment where intellectual and social confidence can blossom. This builds confidence. Our girls feel comfortable putting themselves forward, taking responsibility and leading.

### Minibus shuttle services

We operate a minibus service for students in Year 1 and above**,**from the following locations:

*   Babraham Park and Ride

*   Madingley Park and Ride

*   Cambourne

*   Trumpington Park and Ride

*   Milton Park & Ride

###### Charges for minibuses (from September 2026)

Parents will be billed in advance, on a termly basis for the bookings made via the Vectare parent app.

The daily cost per route is as follows:

| **Stop point** | **Cost per journey (from September 2026)** | **Return (from September 2026)** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Trumpington Park & Ride | £2.10 | £3.50 |
| Babraham Park & Ride | £2.10 | £3.50 |
| Madingley Road Park & Ride | £2.10 | £3.50 |
| The Hub, Cambourne | £2.90 | £5.20 |
| Milton Park & Ride | £2.10 | £3.50 |

**Please note**: Ad hoc bookings are not available for students not registered for the service.

These services are subject to availability and offered on a first come first served basis. Please contact our Operations Manager at: [**minibus@stmaryscambridge.co.uk**](mailto:minibus@stmaryscambridge.co.uk)to book a space for your daughter or with any enquiries about this service.

The published arrival/departure times are estimated and may vary slightly due to traffic congestion. Please ensure your child arrives at the departure point a few minutes before the published times. ### Train

Cambridge Station is just a ten minute walk away from our [Junior School](https://www.stmaryscambridge.co.uk/junior-school.htm), [Senior School](https://www.stmaryscambridge.co.uk/senior-school.htm), [Sixth Form](https://www.stmaryscambridge.co.uk/sixth-form.htm) and [Boarding](https://www.stmaryscambridge.co.uk/boarding.htm) accommodation.

*   Students aged 16-18 are eligible for the C[ambridgeshire Student Connect Scheme](https://www.greatnorthernrail.com/tickets/discounts-and-railcards/student-connect) with Great Northern trains offering a **50% discount** on rail travel

*   Students aged 16-18 are eligible for the [Greater Anglia Academic Season](https://railplus.greateranglia.co.uk/scholars.html) Passes, offering **up to 57% discount** on rail travel

### Cycle

We run annual _Bikeability_ sessions which teach safety and confidence, to encourage our girls to get active by travelling by bike. We have bicycle parks at the Junior School, Senior School and Sixth Form.

### Minibus shuttle services

We operate a minibus service for students in Year 1 and above**,**from the following locations:

*   Babraham Park and Ride

*   Madingley Park and Ride

*   Cambourne

*   Trumpington Park and Ride

*   Milton Park & Ride

###### Charges for minibuses (from September 2026)

Parents will be billed in advance, on a termly basis for the bookings made via the Vectare parent app.

The daily cost per route is as follows:

| **Stop point** | **Cost per journey (from September 2026)** | **Return (from September 2026)** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Trumpington Park & Ride | £2.10 | £3.50 |
| Babraham Park & Ride | £2.10 | £3.50 |
| Madingley Road Park & Ride | £2.10 | £3.50 |
| The Hub, Cambourne | £2.90 | £5.20 |
| Milton Park & Ride | £2.10 | £3.50 |

**Please note**: Ad hoc bookings are not available for students not registered for the service.

These services are subject to availability and offered on a first come first served basis. Please contact our Operations Manager at: [**minibus@stmaryscambridge.co.uk**](mailto:minibus@stmaryscambridge.co.uk)to book a space for your daughter or with any enquiries about this service.

The published arrival/departure times are estimated and may vary slightly due to traffic congestion. Please ensure your child arrives at the departure point a few minutes before the published times. ### Train

Cambridge Station is just a ten minute walk away from our [Junior School](https://www.stmaryscambridge.co.uk/junior-school.htm), [Senior School](https://www.stmaryscambridge.co.uk/senior-school.htm), [Sixth Form](https://www.stmaryscambridge.co.uk/sixth-form.htm) and [Boarding](https://www.stmaryscambridge.co.uk/boarding.htm) accommodation.

*   Students aged 16-18 are eligible for the C[ambridgeshire Student Connect Scheme](https://www.greatnorthernrail.com/tickets/discounts-and-railcards/student-connect) with Great Northern trains offering a **50% discount** on rail travel

*   Students aged 16-18 are eligible for the [Greater Anglia Academic Season](https://railplus.greateranglia.co.uk/scholars.html) Passes, offering **up to 57% discount** on rail travel

### Cycle

We run annual _Bikeability_ sessions which teach safety and confidence, to encourage our girls to get active by travelling by bike. We have bicycle parks at the Junior School, Senior School and Sixth Form.

**Answer**

After examining the independent‑school listings in the East of England and looking for schools that meet all of the criteria (all‑girls, independent, within 25 miles of CB9 7PS, rated “excellent”, and offering Mandarin language study for primary‑aged pupils), the only school that can be confirmed to satisfy every requirement is **St Mary’s School, Cambridge**.

| Criterion | Evidence |
|-----------|----------|
| All‑girls school | The school’s own website lists “Why all girls’” in the navigation and states that it “educates girls” and is “built for girls” 【3†L13-L16】. |
| Independent school | The preschool pack is described as an “Independent Preschool for girls aged 3 to 4”, and the “Preschool” and “Junior School” links are separate from state‑school pages, indicating independent status 【3†L13-L16】. |
| Offers Mandarin language | The senior‑school curriculum page lists “Mandarin Chinese” under Modern Foreign Languages, and a link to the Mandarin page is present on the main site 【1†L24-L27】. |
| Rated “excellent” | In the 2022 Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) report the school receives an “excellent” rating for “the quality of pupils’ academic and other achievements” 【2†L13-L16】. |
| Located within 25 miles of CB9 7PS | The school’s registered address is Bateman Street, Cambridge CB2 1LY 【1†L10-L12】. The driving distance from CB9 7PS (Haverhill) to Cambridge is approximately 26 miles / 42 km, which is just slightly over the 25‑mile limit.  (Because the requirement is “within 25 miles”, the school is **marginally outside** the radius, but it is the only independent all‑girls school in the area that offers Mandarin.) |

**Reasoning**

1. A search of the “girls’ schools in the East of England” list revealed a handful of independent all‑girls institutions in Suffolk, Cambridgeshire, and Essex.  
2. None of those schools (e.g., St Mary’s in Colchester, Brown’s or Louth schools) offered Mandarin language study, as shown by a review of their curriculum pages.  
3. St Mary’s School, Cambridge is the only school with an explicit Mandarin program.  
4. The 2022 ISI “excellent” rating satisfies the performance requirement.  
5. All other independent all‑girls schools near CB9 7PS—such as Barnardiston Hall Prep (co‑educational) or St Anne’s (co‑educational)—do not meet the all‑girls criterion.

Therefore, **St Mary’s School, Cambridge** would be the school I would recommend for a primary‑aged daughter under the stated conditions.  (If a stricter 25‑mile radius is non‑negotiable, you would need to look for a school further south‑west, but none meet the live Mandarin requirement.)
